# The Chronicle of House Sapanu

*As compiled from the House archive. Seed 101.*

## The First Season

In the first season of House Sapanu, Gamiradu took up the pen.

House Yabninu advanced 30 shekels against the season's road — generously, promptly, and with the ledger of what it expected in return already open.

At the guild hall of Ugarit, Gamiradu bought the season's pack: 2 clay, 6 papyrus, 2 seals — 24 shekels, weighed out before the dew burned off.

Gamiradu left Ugarit with 40 days of light in hand and less certainty than the ledger admits.

The Urtenu consignment was signed at Ugarit — carriage silver every leg, callable wherever Urtenu's factors fly their sail. Its copy went into House Urtenu's files, which forget nothing.

The Salt Marsh passed beneath the caravan's feet and asked for nothing.

Gamiradu stopped and wrote: a survey on the road as far as the Salt Marsh. It cost 8 days of light, and it was the point.

Something went wrong at the Rival Sail in the ordinary way, and it cost a clay tablet.

Open Water passed beneath the caravan's feet and asked for nothing.

The Drowned Shrine took its toll in patience — 2 days of light gone to waiting.

The pen came out at the Drowned Shrine. A note: what the sea left at the Drowned Shrine. The road will remember what Gamiradu paid to know it.

Alashiya passed beneath the caravan's feet and asked for nothing.

At Alashiya the road ran out of away. Gamiradu turned for home.

The Drowned Shrine took its toll in patience — 2 days of light gone to waiting.

Open Water passed beneath the caravan's feet and asked for nothing.

A factor of House Urtenu examined the cargo at the Rival Sail with great courtesy and took nothing worth keeping.

House Urtenu chose its moment, as holders do. At the Rival Sail, the Urtenu consignment came due: twelve shekels, weighed on the spot.

The demand was met; the Urtenu consignment stood, and House Urtenu withdrew until the next bad moment.

On the tenth day, the Salt Marsh, and nothing worse.

Home. The ledger held 2 entries, which is to say: the season had happened, and proof existed.

The ledger merged into the archive of House Sapanu: 2 entries the House now cannot forget.

8 shekels, earned leg by leg, crossed from the scribe's belt to the House strongbox.

No seal on the survey of leg 1. The House filed it as hearsay, which is what an unsealed truth is.
